title: Group vocals and The Black Spider on the Decca sides
summary: Lee recalls the Decca sides with the Nat Cole trio's group vocals and the very fast Black Spider.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Yeah. You mentioned that you did 4 or 5 sides with Nat on Decca and one of the things you remember the name of was "The Black Spider" and about the same time you did the measured music things, and you said on those, it was group vocals. Were there also group vocals on the Decca sides?

Uh huh. Yeah, but I can't -- I don't know, that's where we were singing "Sunny Side of the Street" and I was trying to think of the name of the other thing where all of us sang in unison together, and he made some cute little vocal arrangements, you know. Now, I can't remember the name of the song, but it was a standard, too. One of them was a real good arrangement, but I don't recall what it was. But "Black Spider" would stand out in my mind

because it was so fast, you know, and Oscar and Nat had -- you know, it was like 2 parts that they were playing these things real fast, and so the drum and the bass, we were really working to try to keep that thing together. Now that's one record I would like to get, and it's called "Black Spider".
Well, it may still be around Decca someplace.
I don't know ... I may try them one day.
